intent: One action in a context menu, run when the user clicks or presses the row.
typical_uses: A command on the right-clicked element, such as Rename, Duplicate or Delete

dont_use_when.situation: A setting the user turns on or off
One choice out of several mutually exclusive options
A row that opens a further level of actions

instead.target: a link outside the menu, such as the app router's link component
instead.note: The kit exports no link item for this menu; ContextMenuItem renders a div with the menuitem role, not a link.

invariants.text: Activating the item by pointer or by Enter calls `onClick` and closes the whole menu, unless `closeOnClick` is false.
A `disabled` row stays in arrow-key navigation and can take focus, but pressing it or pressing Enter on it does nothing.
The destructive variant draws the text in the danger color at rest and while highlighted; only a light danger tint behind it marks the highlight.

context-menu.module.css sizes every descendant `svg` of the row to the small icon size and keeps it from shrinking or taking pointer events, so a leading icon passed in children needs no size of its own.
`inset` indents the item's text by the width of the icon column (the small icon size plus two spacing steps), so a row without an icon lines up with rows that start with one.

anti_patterns.dont: Mark a reversible or everyday action with `variant="destructive"`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep `destructive` for an action that deletes or cannot be undone, so the red row stays a warning

a11y.by: context-menu.test.tsx asserts the item is found by role menuitem and its accessible name, that a disabled item carries data-disabled, and that clicking an item removes the menu

onClick.states: onClick is a callback called with the click event when the item is activated by pointer or keyboard
onClick.because: A React event handler - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the item's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, highlighted). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: An action with an icon and a shortcut hint
A destructive action and a disabled one

bad.title: A made-up onSelect handler for the action
bad.why: The item has no `onSelect` prop; the name falls through to the forwarded `<div>` as the DOM's text-selection event, which a click on the row never fires. Run the action from `onClick`.
